scope: User review of round 152–162 wording: East Slavic names, early Soviet abbreviation names, coined and literary names.
decisions: Do not call a name Russian, Ukrainian or Belarusian; use East Slavic or Slavic for modern forms and Kyivan Rus for historical ones, with the ultimate origin added. Cognate lists and historical facts stay.
Early Soviet abbreviation names are written as riddles that hint at their source without naming it.

Coined and literary names show where they came from; Rigonda and Leho already did, and Leho gets a supplement on Lehola. The user's suggested link of Leho with leht (leaf) was not added because the records point to Lehola and Leonhard.
Ask the user with a full worked example before changing these wording rules again.
method: namedays-plain-r163.js: sentence map W163 (merged into the round 140 map) and finalWording() for root and family histories that bypass the sentence map; namedays-hypotheses-r163.js overrides earlier hypotheses for Vilens, Kima, Revs and Rema; namedays-hypotheses-supplements-r163.js adds labelled supplements. A full scan of displayed EN and RU text (var/namedays-research/scan163.mjs, scanru163.mjs) found the remaining cases; what remains are cognate lists and historical facts.
other_fixes: Russian “дистрицт” mistranslations of “district” in five research texts replaced with proper district names (Елгавский, Огрский, Добельский, Рижский район).
Ruslans: arslan is Turkic, not Arabic.

records.name: Roksolana
